Module 3: Question features in XLSForm

Download the template

Open msn_xlsform_template.xlsx and follow along. It has the three sheets, the metadata rows, the correct bilingual column headers, and a complete worked example. Always start from this file instead of a blank Excel sheet. The instructions sheet inside it is ignored by KoboToolbox. Most features below are used in that file.

Required questions

Write yes in the required column. The form will not continue until the question is answered.

type name label required
integer age Age (completed years) yes

Make key questions (outcome, main exposure, consent) required. Leave optional questions, such as comments, not required.

Grouping questions (begin_group / end_group)

Groups organise your questionnaire into sections, like Section A, B, C in your questionnaire.

type name label appearance
begin_group demographics Section A: Socio-demographic information field-list
integer age Age (completed years)
select_one sex sex Sex
end_group demographics
  • Every begin_group must have a matching end_group.
  • appearance = field-list shows all questions of the group on one screen.
  • A relevant condition on begin_group applies to the whole group.

Question skipping (skip logic with relevant)

The relevant column says when a question should appear. Refer to an earlier question with ${name}.

type name label relevant
select_one occupation occupation Main occupation
text occupation_other Please specify other occupation ${occupation} = 'other'
select_multiple symptoms symptoms Symptoms in the last 7 days
integer fever_days Days of fever selected(${symptoms}, 'fever')

Common patterns:

Situation relevant expression
Show if answer is “yes” ${consent} = 'yes'
Show if age is 60 or above ${age} >= 60
Show if an option is ticked in a multiple choice selected(${symptoms}, 'fever')
Show if female and married ${sex} = 'female' and ${marital} = 'married'
Show if either condition ${diabetes} = 'yes' or ${hypertension} = 'yes'
Warning

Text values need single quotes ('yes'). Numbers do not (${age} >= 60). The value must be the choice name, not the label ('yes', not 'Yes' or 'हो').

Accepting only certain values (constraint)

A constraint checks the answer before the respondent can continue. The dot . means “this question’s answer”.

type name label constraint constraint_message
integer age Age (completed years) . >= 30 and . <= 80 Age must be between 30 and 80 years.
decimal weight Weight (kg) . >= 20 and . <= 200 Weight must be between 20 and 200 kg.
date admission_date Date of admission . <= today() Date cannot be in the future.

Useful constraints:

Purpose constraint
Range 30 to 80 . >= 30 and . <= 80
Not in the future . <= today()
Cannot be more than the age . <= ${age}
“None” cannot be selected with other options not(selected(., 'none') and count-selected(.) > 1)
Maximum 3 options ticked count-selected(.) <= 3

For a bilingual form, add a constraint_message::Nepali (ne) column as well, so the error message appears in both languages.

Tip

Use your inclusion criteria as constraints. If your study includes adults aged 30–80, the form should make it impossible to enter 25 or 95.

Calculations (calculate)

A calculate row works out a value automatically. It is not shown to the respondent, but it is saved in the data.

type name label calculation
decimal weight Weight (kg)
decimal height Height (cm)
calculate bmi round(${weight} div pow(${height} div 100, 2), 1)
note bmi_note BMI: ${bmi} kg/m²
  • Use div for division and pow(number, power) for powers. / and ^ don’t work in XLSForm.
  • Show a calculated value to the respondent by writing ${name} inside a note label.
  • Type formulas by hand rather than pasting them from Word, so no hidden characters or curly quotes get in.

Likert scale

Create the scale once in choices, then reuse it for every item. Use appearance = likert to display the options in a row.

choices

list_name name label::English (en) label::Nepali (ne)
agree5 1 Strongly disagree पूर्ण असहमत
agree5 2 Disagree असहमत
agree5 3 Neutral तटस्थ
agree5 4 Agree सहमत
agree5 5 Strongly agree पूर्ण सहमत

survey

type name label::English (en) appearance calculation
begin_group satisfaction Section C: Satisfaction with nursing care field-list
select_one agree5 sat1 Nurses explained procedures clearly. likert
select_one agree5 sat2 Nurses responded promptly when I needed help. likert
select_one agree5 sat3 I was treated with respect and dignity. likert
end_group satisfaction
  • Using numbers 1–5 as choice names makes scoring easy.
  • The calculate row adds up the three items into a total score automatically.
  • For negatively worded items, reverse the score at analysis, or use a separate list where “Strongly disagree” = 5.
  • To show all items as one grid instead, use table-list on begin_group (see Appearance in the tips below).
TipXLSForm tips and tricks

Most upload errors come from a few small mistakes. Check these before you upload your form.

The name column

  • No spaces. Use an underscore instead: marital_status, not marital status.
  • Start with a letter, not a number: q1_age, not 1_age.
  • Use only letters, numbers and underscores. No hyphens, dots, brackets or Nepali characters.
  • Every name must be unique in the survey sheet.
  • Keep names short and meaningful, in lowercase: hb_level is better than x7 or Haemoglobin_Level_Of_Patient.
  • Don’t rename a question after data collection starts. KoboToolbox treats the new name as a new question, and your data will be split into two columns.

The choices sheet

  • The list_name must match exactly the word after select_one or select_multiple in the survey sheet, including spelling and capital letters.
  • Choice names follow the same rules: no spaces, unique within the list.
  • Reuse lists. One yes_no list can serve every yes/no question.
  • For Likert scales, use numbers as choice names (1 to 5) to make scoring easy.
  • Add “Other” with a follow-up text question shown only when “Other” is selected.
  • Use fixed codes for special answers and keep them the same in every list, for example 98 = Don’t know, 99 = Refused.
  • Don’t change choice names after deployment. You can edit labels, but changing names makes old and new data inconsistent.

Skip logic and constraints

  • Refer to other questions as ${name}, spelled exactly as in the name column.
  • Put text values in single quotes (${consent} = 'yes'). Numbers don’t need quotes (${age} >= 18).
  • Use the choice name, not the label: 'yes', not 'Yes' or 'हो'.
  • For select_multiple, use selected(${symptoms}, 'fever'), not ${symptoms} = 'fever'.
  • In a constraint, . means the current answer: . >= 30 and . <= 80.
  • Write and / or in lowercase.
  • Always add a constraint_message, so the data collector knows what went wrong.

Structure

  • Sheet names must be exactly survey, choices and settings, in lowercase.
  • Column headers must be spelled exactly (constraint_message, not constraint message).
  • Every begin_group needs a matching end_group.
  • Don’t merge cells or use Excel formulas in the form.
  • Every question needs a label, except calculate rows and metadata (start, end, today, deviceid).

Multiple languages

  • Write language names identically in every column: label::Nepali (ne) everywhere, never Nepali (ne) in one column and nepali(ne) in another.
  • Fill in every language column for every question, including hints, constraint messages and choices.
  • Type Nepali in Unicode (Nepali Unicode keyboard). Preeti and other old fonts display as random letters on phones.
  • Set default_language in the settings sheet.

Appearance: change how a question looks

The appearance column changes how a question or group is displayed, without changing the data that are saved. Common appearances:

appearance Use with What it does
field-list begin_group Shows all questions of the group on one screen
table-list begin_group Shows questions with the same answer options as a grid
likert select_one Shows options in a row, like a rating scale
minimal select_one / select_multiple Shows options in a drop-down list, useful for long lists
multiline text Gives a larger box for long answers
month-year date Asks only for month and year, e.g. when the exact date isn’t known
  • More appearances Appearances can look slightly different in the web form and in KoboCollect, so always preview your form. For the full list with examples, see the XLSForm appearance reference.

Testing and versions

Check your form online before uploading XLSForm Online is a free tool from ODK that checks your XLSForm for errors, without needing a KoboToolbox account.

  1. Go to https://getodk.org/xlsform/.
  2. Click Choose file and select your .xlsx form.
  3. Click Submit.
  4. If there are errors, a message appears with the row number and the problem. Fix it in Excel, save, and submit again.
  5. When the form has no errors, click Preview in browser to fill in the form as a respondent would, and test the skip logic, constraints and language switch.

XLSForm Online uses the same XLSForm rules as KoboToolbox, so most errors show up here first. Always do a final check in KoboToolbox before deploying, as a few display options can look slightly different there.

  • Preview the form in KoboToolbox before deploying, and test the skip logic, constraints and language switch.
  • Submit test data with wrong values on purpose, to check that your constraints work.
  • Increase the version in the settings sheet every time you change and re-upload the form.
  • Save each version with a new file name (survey_v1.xlsx, survey_v2.xlsx), so you can go back if something breaks.
  • Delete all test submissions before real data collection starts.
WarningExcel traps
  • Curly quotes: Excel may change 'yes' into ‘yes’, and KoboToolbox won’t accept curly quotes. In Windows Excel, turn this off under File → Options → Proofing → AutoCorrect Options → AutoFormat As You Type, and untick “Straight quotes with smart quotes”.
  • Extra spaces: a space at the end of a cell (sex) is invisible but breaks the link between list_name and select_one sex.
  • Automatic dates: Excel may turn entries like 1-5 into a date. Format those cells as Text before typing.
TipStuck on an error?

Read the error message carefully. It usually names the row number and the problem. Also check the course template: if your form works differently from the example, compare the two row by row.

Quiz: question features

For each question, click the answer you think is correct. Then press Check answers.
